text: The solubility of AgCN in a buffer solution of pH = 3 is x. The value of x is : [Assume : No cyano complex is formed; $K_{sp}($AgCN) = 2.2 $\times$ $10^{-16}$ and $K_{a}($HCN) = 6.2 $\times$ $10^{-10}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a buffer of pH 3, $[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]=10^{-3}\text{M}$, which is far larger than $K_{a}(\mathrm{HCN})=6.2\times 10^{-10}$. Hence $\dfrac{[\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}]}{[\mathrm{HCN}]}=\dfrac{K_{a}}{[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]}=6.2\times 10^{-7}$, so almost all the cyanide released is present as HCN.

The overall equilibrium is $\mathrm{AgCN}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}+\mathrm{HCN}$, with $K=\dfrac{K_{sp}}{K_{a}}$.

With solubility $x$: $[\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}]=x$ and $[\mathrm{HCN}]\approx x$, while $[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]$ is fixed by the buffer.

$\frac{x\cdot x}{[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]}=\frac{K_{sp}}{K_{a}}\Rightarrow x^{2}=\frac{K_{sp}[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]}{K_{a}}=\frac{2.2\times 10^{-16}\times 10^{-3}}{6.2\times 10^{-10}}=3.55\times 10^{-10}$

$x=1.88\times 10^{-5}\approx 1.9\times 10^{-5}\text{M}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text:
The plots of radial distribution functions for various orbitals of hydrogen atom against 'r' are given below :


[IMG]


The correct plot for 3s orbital is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Number of radial nodes $=n-l-1$. For 3s, $n=3$ and $l=0$, so there are $3-0-1=2$ radial nodes: the radial distribution curve has three maxima, and between them it falls to zero at two values of $r$ (the zero at $r=0$ is not a node).

Plot (A) has a single maximum near $0.53$ Å and no node (1s). Plot (B) has two maxima with one zero between them, i.e. one radial node (2s). Plot (C) has a single maximum near $2.1$ Å and no node (2p).

Plot (D) has three maxima with the curve touching zero at two points between them, i.e. two radial nodes, as required for 3s. Plot (D) is given as option (D).

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: According to molecular orbital theory, the species among the following that does not exist is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Note :

According to molecular orbital theory, when a molecule have bond order = 0 then that molecule does not exist.

We know, Bond order $=\frac{1}{2}$ [$N_{b}$ $-$ $N_{a}$] 

$N_{b} =$ No of electrons in bonding molecular orbital 

$N_{a}$ $=$ No of electrons in anti bonding molecular orbital 

(4) $\, ~$ upto 14 electrons, molecular orbital configuration is 


[IMG]


Here $N_{a} =$ Anti bonding electron $=$ 4 and $N_{b} = 10$

(5) $\, ~$ After 14  electrons to 20 electrons molecular orbital configuration is - - -


[IMG]


Here $N_{a} = 10$

and $N_{b} = 10$

Molecular orbital configuration of O ${}_{2}^{2-}$ (18 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 8$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}$ [ 10 $-$ 8] = 1
 

$\, ~$ Configuration of $He_{2}^{+}$ (3 electrons) is = $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{1}}^{\ast }$ 

$\therefore \quad$ Bond order = $\frac{1}{2}$ (2 $-$1) = 0.5

$\, ~$ Configuration of $He_{2}^{-}$ (5 electrons) is = $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{1}}$ 

$\therefore \quad$ Bond order = $\frac{1}{2}$ (3 $-$2) = 0.5

$\, ~$ Configuration of $Be_{2}$ (8 electrons) is = $σ_{1s^{2}}$ $σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }$ $σ_{2s^{2}}$ $σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore$ Bond order = $\frac{1}{2}$ (4 $-$ 4) = 0

text: 0.4 g mixture of NaOH, $Na_{2}CO_{3}$ and some inert impurities was first titrated with $\frac{N}{10}$ HCl using phenolphthalein as an indicator, 17.5 mL of HCl was required at the end point. After this methyl orange was added and titrated. 1.5 mL of same HCl was required for the next end point. The weight percentage of $Na_{2}CO_{3}$ in the mixture is $________. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With phenolphthalein, HCl neutralises all the NaOH but converts $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}$ only to $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$:

$\mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O},\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}+\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}+\mathrm{NaCl}$

$n_{\mathrm{NaOH}}+n_{\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}}=17.5\times 0.1=1.75\text{mmol}$

With methyl orange, the $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$ formed from $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}$ is neutralised:

$\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}+\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$

$n_{\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}}=n_{\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}}=1.5\times 0.1=0.15\text{mmol}$

$\text{Mass of}\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}=0.15\times 10^{-3}\times 106=0.0159\text{g}$

$\text{Percentage of}\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}=\dfrac{0.0159}{0.4}\times 100=3.975%\approx 4%$

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: In basic medium $CrO_{4}^{2-}$ oxidises $S_{2}O_{3}^{2-}$ to form $SO_{4}^{2-}$ and itself changes into $Cr(OH)_{4}^{-}$. The volume of 0.154 M $CrO_{4}^{2-}$ required to react with 40 mL of 0.25 M $S_{2}O_{3}^{2-}$ is $__________ mL. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cr goes from $+6$ in $\mathrm{CrO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ to $+3$ in $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}{}^{-}$, gaining 3 electrons per ion.

S goes from $+2$ in $\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ to $+6$ in $\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$; with two S atoms per ion, each $\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ loses 8 electrons.

Equating electrons gives the balanced equation

$8~\mathrm{CrO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}+3\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}{}^{2-}+17\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow 8\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}{}^{-}+6\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}+2\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$

$n(\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}{}^{2-})=40\times 0.25=10\text{mmol}$, so $n(\mathrm{CrO}{}_{4}{}^{2-})=\dfrac{8}{3}\times 10=26.67\text{mmol}$.

$V=\dfrac{26.67\text{mmol}}{0.154\text{mmol mL}^{-1}}=173.2\text{mL}$

Hence, the answer is 173.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

The number of $sp^{2}$ hybridized carbon atom(s) present in the product is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acetylene passed through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K trimerises to benzene:

$3~\mathrm{HC}\equiv \mathrm{CH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}$

Benzene with CO and HCl in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$ (Gattermann–Koch reaction) gives benzaldehyde, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CHO}$.

In benzaldehyde the six ring carbons are sp${}^{2}$, and the carbonyl carbon of $-\mathrm{CHO}$ (trigonal, with a C=O double bond) is also sp${}^{2}$.

Number of sp${}^{2}$ carbons $=6+1=7$.

Hence, the answer is 7.

text:
Among the following, the number of halide(s) which is/are inert to hydrolysis is $_________$.

$(A) BF_{3}$

(B) SiCl$_{4}$

(C) PCl$_{5}$

$(D) SF_{6}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hydrolysis of a covalent halide needs a site on the central atom that a water molecule can attack.

$\mathrm{BF}{}_{3}$: boron has a vacant 2p orbital, so it is hydrolysed: $4~\mathrm{BF}{}_{3}+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{BO}{}_{3}+3\mathrm{HBF}{}_{4}$.

$\mathrm{SiCl}{}_{4}$: silicon accepts the lone pair of water into its vacant 3d orbitals: $\mathrm{SiCl}{}_{4}+4\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Si}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}+4\mathrm{HCl}$.

$\mathrm{PCl}{}_{5}$: phosphorus is attacked in the same way: $\mathrm{PCl}{}_{5}+4\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{PO}{}_{4}+5\mathrm{HCl}$.

$\mathrm{SF}{}_{6}$: sulphur is coordinatively saturated and sterically shielded by six fluorine atoms, so water cannot reach it and $\mathrm{SF}{}_{6}$ is inert to hydrolysis.

Only $\mathrm{SF}{}_{6}$ is inert to hydrolysis.

Hence, the answer is 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift
